findings: ⚠️ THE CANARY EARNED ITS KEEP. Folding ONE tradition surfaced `harbored_flame` — a `cross_pole_braid` craft living inside a tradition file and covered by nothing. A sweep found 9 uncovered of 285. They were missed for a real reason: I authored BY TRADITION and these sit OUTSIDE the 27. Finding this at tradition 1 instead of tradition 27 is the entire argument for canarying a big change.

AND THEY ARE NOT FILLER — they are arguably the most important nine crafts in the game. The 6 precursor arts are the T3-T5 SPINE of the whole precursor layer (the thing SNG-261 §B has been trying to wire), and the 3 braids are the ONLY crafts requiring TWO poles.

⚠️ CCODE — DUAL-POLE GATING IS NOW A REAL CATEGORY, NOT AN EDGE CASE. Checks item 6e logged it from ONE instance (somatic's the_whole_act). There are now FOUR: all three braids carry `requiresPoles`, and the engine cannot express any of them. Worth building properly rather than special-casing.

⚠️ A TWENTIETH DEFENSIVE LOGIC — HELD-OPEN (`hold_the_aperture`): soak 0, because it does not stop harm, it stops a thing from CLOSING. The only guard in 285 crafts whose subject is A POSSIBILITY rather than a person.

⚠️ AND THE PAIR AT THE TOP OF THE PRECURSOR LADDER IS ERIK'S FRAMEWORK, MADE CASTABLE: `foreclose` (T-IV) closes a possibility and DRIFTS YOU, with the drift ACCELERATING — foreclosure being his own definition of evil. `hold_the_aperture` (T-V) is the same power spent to keep something OPEN, at continuous cost. And the game's own text calls THAT one 'the hardest thing in the game' — not the one that unmakes, but the one that refuses to let something close.
